newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi index falls on low pace trading.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi index falls on low pace trading.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index continued a downward spiral on Monday on a continued drop in leading companies, brokers said.
The index fell 1.24 points to stand at 3048.61. Turnover was posted at 9.573 million shillings on 290,083 shares from 10.043 million shillings on 346,637 shares on Friday.
A senior broker said some counters came down on poor buying support and news was lacking to excite the market.
Barclays Bank of Kenya shed 2.0 shillings to 100, Diamond Trust fell to 37 from 38 while National Bank of Kenya traded 49,125 shares at 17.45, 16.60 and 16.80 from 17.65.
Brokers said Kenya Commercial Bank, in which the government offered for sale a further 11.88 million primary shares or 10 percent of its stake on Monday, had good trading.
The price for each primary share is 50 shillings.
"Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB) is a popular counter. There is good buying and selling support for the stock. It has attracted a lot of interest from investors," one broker said.
KCB traded a total of 34,417 shares at 55.50 from 54.50 on Friday.
Among the Plantations, Kakuzi rose to 95 from 92.50, Rea Vipingo eased to 10.95 from 11 while Brooke Bond was unchanged at 177.
Most commercials held steady: Nation Printers & Publishers at 104, Uchumi Supermarket at 38 while Kenya Airways eased to 11 shillings from 11.20 on 99,011 shares.
Firestone East Africa fell to 24 from 24.25.
Bourse officials said foreign investors dealt 2,000 shares of Kenya Breweries at 46.50 from 46 previously.
